17 18 # FRAI · Framework of Responsible Artificial Intelligence 19 20 ![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/frai) 21 ![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/frai) 22 23 **Live platform:** [frai.cc](https://www.frai.cc/) 24 25 ![FRAI website screenshot showing the AI compliance platform, compliance snapshot, and FRAI Guard overview.](assets/frai_cc_screenshot.png) 26 27 FRAI is an open-source toolkit that helps teams launch AI features responsibly. It guides you through evidence gathering, scans your code, and assembles documentation you can hand to reviewers: implementation checklists, model cards, risk files, evaluation reports, and compliance-aware RAG indexes. The toolkit ships as four packages that work together: 28 29 - `frai` – the command-line app with ready-to-run workflows. 30 - `frai-core` – the reusable SDK that powers the CLI and any custom integrations. 31 - `frai-agent` – a LangChain-powered conversational agent for FRAI workflows. 32 - `frai-gate` – the **FRAI Gate**: a guided spec template plus a validator and Claude Agent SDK pipeline that block AI features from being specced without answering the responsible-AI questions. (The matching agent skill lives in [frai-skills](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills).) 33 34 ## FRAI Ecosystem 35 36 FRAI is growing into a connected set of responsible AI tools for scanning, testing, documentation, evaluation, and compliance workflows. 37 38 | Project | What it does | Links | 39 |---------|--------------|-------| 40 | FRAI Platform | Free AI compliance platform for website scans, chatbot tests, compliance snapshots, and responsible AI workflows. | [Website](https://www.frai.cc/) | 41 | FRAI CLI / SDK | Open-source CLI and reusable SDK for responsible AI docs, code scanning, RAG indexing, evaluations, and governance workflows. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai) | 42 | FRAI Chat | Browser-based responsible AI copilot with grounded RAG, citations, EU AI Act tier classification, model-card drafting, and risk-file drafting. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-chat) · [Live demo](https://sebuzdugan.github.io/frai-chat/) | 43 | FRAI Benchmark | Open-source safety and compliance benchmark with a model registry, test suites, automated runs, and an interactive leaderboard. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-benchmark) · [Leaderboard](https://sebuzdugan.github.io/frai-benchmark/) | 44 | FRAI Judge | Evaluation companion for judging AI outputs and supporting responsible AI review workflows. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-judge) | 45 | FRAI Skills | Agent skills for responsible AI engineering - the FRAI Gate spec workflow for AI coding agents (`npx skills add sebuzdugan/frai-skills`). | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills) | 46 47 ### Short Answer 48 - `frai-core` is the library/SDK. Use it when you are embedding FRAI capabilities into your own tools, servers, automations, or extensions. 49 - `frai` is the CLI. It wraps `frai-core` to deliver an end-user experience with no coding required. 50 51 ### Why Keep Both? 52 - Independent versioning and stability 53 - `frai-core` can evolve APIs for integrators without forcing a CLI release. 54 - `frai` can improve UX/commands without breaking programmatic users. 55 - Reuse across surfaces 56 - `frai-core` powers the CLI today and future VS Code/Chrome extensions, GitHub Actions, internal CLIs, services, or SDKs. 57 - Smaller, focused installs 58 - Operators install the CLI. 59 - Builders install only the core library they need. 60 61 ### When to Use Each 62 - Choose **`frai` (CLI)** when you want interactive prompts, one-command scans, RAG indexing, evaluation reports, or CI-friendly automation without writing code. 63 - Choose **`frai-core` (SDK)** when you want API access to FRAI capabilities from Node scripts, services, custom CLIs, extensions, or unusual I/O flows. 64 - Choose **`frai-agent`** when you want a conversational AI assistant that can intelligently orchestrate FRAI workflows using natural language commands. 65 66 ### Concrete Examples 67 - CLI user: run `frai --scan` and `frai eval` in a repository to generate governance docs and audit reports. 68 - Library user: call `Documents.generateDocuments` from an internal portal to produce standardized docs, use `Scanners.scanCodebase` inside a GitHub Action, or embed `Rag.indexDocuments` inside a VS Code extension for grounded hints. 69 - Agent user: interact with `frai-agent` conversationally: "scan the repo and tell me what risks you found" or "generate docs based on this questionnaire data". 70 71 In short: CLI = product; Core = platform. They overlap in capability on purpose but target different audiences and distribution needs. 72 73 --- 74 75 ## Getting Started with the CLI 76 77 1. Install the published CLI: 78 ```bash 79 npm install -g frai 80 ``` 81 2. Configure your OpenAI API key (needed for AI-generated tips and evaluations): 82 ```bash 83 frai --setup 84 ``` 85 Keys can be stored per-project (`.env`) or globally (`~/.config/frai/config`). You can also provide a one-off key using `frai --key sk-...`. 86 3. Run the interactive workflow: 87 ```bash 88 frai 89 ``` 90 FRAI walks you through feature discovery, writes `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`, and optionally exports PDFs. 91 92 Generated artefacts live in your current working directory. Supplementary commands cover scanning, evaluation, RAG indexing, and fine-tuning governance. 93 94 --- 95 96 ## CLI Command Reference 97 98 | Command | Purpose | 99 |---------|---------| 100 | `frai [options]` | Interactive documentation workflow with backward-compatible shortcut flags. | 101 | `frai generate [options]` | Explicit interactive workflow command. | 102 | `frai scan [--ci] [--json]` | Scan the repository for AI/ML indicators. | 103 | `frai setup [--key ] [--global]` | Store an OpenAI API key locally or globally. | 104 | `frai config` | Show key configuration status. | 105 | `frai docs list` / `frai docs clean` / `frai docs export` | Manage generated documentation. | 106 | `frai rag index [options]` | Build a local compliance-aware vector index. | 107 | `frai eval --outputs [...]` | Run baseline evaluation metrics and write reports. | 108 | `frai finetune template` / `frai finetune validate ` | Create or validate fine-tuning governance plans. | 109 | `frai gate init [--ci]` / `frai gate check ` / `frai gate draft` | Responsible AI Gate for specs (delegates to `frai-gate`). | 110 | `frai update` | Check npm for the latest CLI release. | 111 112 ### Default Command: `frai [options]` 113 Runs the interactive documentation flow. Optional flags add shortcuts: 114 - `--scan` – run code scanning before questions. 115 - `--ci` – exit after scanning when no AI indicators are detected. 116 - `--setup` – jump directly into key configuration. 117 - `--key ` / `--global` – provide a key and optionally persist it globally. 118 - `--list-docs` / `--clean` – list or remove generated docs. 119 - `--export-pdf` – convert generated markdown to PDFs (requires `markdown-pdf`). 120 - `--show-config` – display key storage status. 121 - `--update` – check npm for a newer CLI version. 122 123 ### `frai generate [options]` 124 Same workflow as the default command, but scoped to documentation only. Options mirror the defaults: `--scan`, `--ci`, `--key`, `--global`, `--export-pdf`, and `--show-config`. 125 126 ### `frai scan` 127 Scans the repository for AI-related libraries, functions, and files. Use `--ci` for non-interactive mode or `--json` to emit raw JSON. 128 129 ### `frai setup` 130 Guided API key storage. Supply `--key ` for headless use and `--global` to persist at `~/.config/frai/config`. 131 132 ### `frai config` 133 Prints whether local (`.env`) or global configuration holds an API key. 134 135 ### `frai docs` 136 Utilities for generated artefacts: 137 - `frai docs list` – list detected `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`. 138 - `frai docs clean` – delete generated docs. 139 - `frai docs export` – export docs to PDF via `markdown-pdf`. 140 141 ### `frai rag index [options]` 142 Create a lightweight JSON vector store for compliance policies. 143 - `--input ` – file or directory to index (defaults to cwd). 144 - `--output ` – target JSON file (defaults to `frai-index.json`). 145 - `--chunk-size ` – words per chunk (default 800). 146 - `--extensions ` – allowlisted extensions (default `.md,.markdown,.txt,.json,.yaml,.yml`). 147 148 ### `frai eval` 149 Generate evaluation reports for model outputs. 150 - `--outputs ` *(required)* – JSON file with model outputs. 151 - `--references ` – JSON file with reference answers. 152 - `--report ` – output location (`frai-eval-report.json` by default). 153 - `--format ` – output format (defaults to JSON). Markdown reports include human-readable summaries for review boards. 154 155 ### `frai finetune` 156 Fine-tuning governance helpers: 157 - `frai finetune template [--output ]` – write a governance template JSON (`frai-finetune-plan.json` by default). 158 - `frai finetune validate [--readiness]` – validate a plan and optionally print readiness checkpoints and summaries. 159 160 ### `frai update` 161 Check npm for the latest `frai` release and print upgrade instructions. 162 163 --- 164 165 ## Using `frai-core` (SDK) 166 167 Install from npm: 168 ```bash 169 pnpm add frai-core 170 ``` 171 172 `frai-core` exposes modular helpers that the CLI uses under the hood: 173 - `Questionnaire` – interactive question flows. 174 - `Documents` – generate checklists, model cards, and risk files. 175 - `Scanners` – static analysis for AI indicators. 176 - `Rag` – policy-grounded indexing utilities. 177 - `Eval` – baseline evaluation metrics and report writers. 178 - `Finetune` – governance templates, validation, and readiness scoring. 179 - `Config` & `Providers` – key management and LLM provider wiring. 180 181 Example: generate documentation programmatically. 182 183 ```ts 184 import fs from 'fs/promises'; 185 import inquirer from 'inquirer'; 186 import { Documents, Questionnaire, Scanners } from 'frai-core'; 187 188 const answers = await Questionnaire.runQuestionnaire({ 189 prompt: (questions) => inquirer.prompt(questions) 190 }); 191 192 const { checklist, modelCard, riskFile } = Documents.generateDocuments({ answers }); 193 const scan = Scanners.scanCodebase({ root: process.cwd() }); 194 const aiContext = Documents.buildContextForAITips(answers); 17 18 # FRAI · Framework of Responsible Artificial Intelligence 19 20 ![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/frai) 21 ![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/frai) 22 23 24 FRAI is an open-source toolkit that helps teams launch AI features responsibly. It guides you through evidence gathering, scans your code, and assembles documentation you can hand to reviewers: implementation checklists, model cards, risk files, evaluation reports, and compliance-aware RAG indexes. The toolkit ships as two packages that work together: 25 26 - `frai` – the command-line app with ready-to-run workflows. 27 - `frai-core` – the reusable SDK that powers the CLI and any custom integrations. 28 29 ### Short Answer 30 - `frai-core` is the library/SDK. Use it when you are embedding FRAI capabilities into your own tools, servers, automations, or extensions. 31 - `frai` is the CLI. It wraps `frai-core` to deliver an end-user experience with no coding required. 32 33 ### Why Keep Both? 34 - Independent versioning and stability 35 - `frai-core` can evolve APIs for integrators without forcing a CLI release. 36 - `frai` can improve UX/commands without breaking programmatic users. 37 - Reuse across surfaces 38 - `frai-core` powers the CLI today and future VS Code/Chrome extensions, GitHub Actions, internal CLIs, services, or SDKs. 39 - Smaller, focused installs 40 - Operators install the CLI. 41 - Builders install only the core library they need. 42 43 ### When to Use Each 44 - Choose **`frai` (CLI)** when you want interactive prompts, one-command scans, RAG indexing, evaluation reports, or CI-friendly automation without writing code. 45 - Choose **`frai-core` (SDK)** when you want API access to FRAI capabilities from Node scripts, services, custom CLIs, extensions, or unusual I/O flows. 46 47 ### Concrete Examples 48 - CLI user: run `frai --scan` and `frai eval` in a repository to generate governance docs and audit reports. 49 - Library user: call `Documents.generateDocuments` from an internal portal to produce standardized docs, use `Scanners.scanCodebase` inside a GitHub Action, or embed `Rag.indexDocuments` inside a VS Code extension for grounded hints. 50 51 In short: CLI = product; Core = platform. They overlap in capability on purpose but target different audiences and distribution needs. 52 53 --- 54 55 ## Getting Started with the CLI 56 57 1. Install the published CLI: 58 ```bash 59 npm install -g frai 60 ``` 61 2. Configure your OpenAI API key (needed for AI-generated tips and evaluations): 62 ```bash 63 frai --setup 64 ``` 65 Keys can be stored per-project (`.env`) or globally (`~/.config/frai/config`). You can also provide a one-off key using `frai --key sk-...`. 66 3. Run the interactive workflow: 67 ```bash 68 frai 69 ``` 70 FRAI walks you through feature discovery, writes `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`, and optionally exports PDFs. 71 72 Generated artefacts live in your current working directory. Supplementary commands cover scanning, evaluation, RAG indexing, and fine-tuning governance. 73 74 --- 75 76 ## CLI Command Reference 77 78 | Command | Purpose | 79 |---------|---------| 80 | `frai [options]` | Interactive documentation workflow with backward-compatible shortcut flags. | 81 | `frai generate [options]` | Explicit interactive workflow command. | 82 | `frai scan [--ci] [--json]` | Scan the repository for AI/ML indicators. | 83 | `frai setup [--key ] [--global]` | Store an OpenAI API key locally or globally. | 84 | `frai config` | Show key configuration status. | 85 | `frai docs list` / `frai docs clean` / `frai docs export` | Manage generated documentation. | 86 | `frai rag index [options]` | Build a local compliance-aware vector index. | 87 | `frai eval --outputs [...]` | Run baseline evaluation metrics and write reports. | 88 | `frai finetune template` / `frai finetune validate ` | Create or validate fine-tuning governance plans. | 89 | `frai update` | Check npm for the latest CLI release. | 90 91 ### Default Command: `frai [options]` 92 Runs the interactive documentation flow. Optional flags add shortcuts: 93 - `--scan` – run code scanning before questions. 94 - `--ci` – exit after scanning when no AI indicators are detected. 95 - `--setup` – jump directly into key configuration. 96 - `--key ` / `--global` – provide a key and optionally persist it globally. 97 - `--list-docs` / `--clean` – list or remove generated docs. 98 - `--export-pdf` – convert generated markdown to PDFs (requires `markdown-pdf`). 99 - `--show-config` – display key storage status. 100 - `--update` – check npm for a newer CLI version. 101 102 ### `frai generate [options]` 103 Same workflow as the default command, but scoped to documentation only. Options mirror the defaults: `--scan`, `--ci`, `--key`, `--global`, `--export-pdf`, and `--show-config`. 104 105 ### `frai scan` 106 Scans the repository for AI-related libraries, functions, and files. Use `--ci` for non-interactive mode or `--json` to emit raw JSON. 107 108 ### `frai setup` 109 Guided API key storage. Supply `--key ` for headless use and `--global` to persist at `~/.config/frai/config`. 110 111 ### `frai config` 112 Prints whether local (`.env`) or global configuration holds an API key. 113 114 ### `frai docs` 115 Utilities for generated artefacts: 116 - `frai docs list` – list detected `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`. 117 - `frai docs clean` – delete generated docs. 118 - `frai docs export` – export docs to PDF via `markdown-pdf`. 119 120 ### `frai rag index [options]` 121 Create a lightweight JSON vector store for compliance policies. 122 - `--input ` – file or directory to index (defaults to cwd). 123 - `--output ` – target JSON file (defaults to `frai-index.json`). 124 - `--chunk-size ` – words per chunk (default 800). 125 - `--extensions ` – allowlisted extensions (default `.md,.markdown,.txt,.json,.yaml,.yml`). 126 127 ### `frai eval` 128 Generate evaluation reports for model outputs. 129 - `--outputs ` *(required)* – JSON file with model outputs. 130 - `--references ` – JSON file with reference answers. 131 - `--report ` – output location (`frai-eval-report.json` by default). 132 - `--format ` – output format (defaults to JSON). Markdown reports include human-readable summaries for review boards. 133 134 ### `frai finetune` 135 Fine-tuning governance helpers: 136 - `frai finetune template [--output ]` – write a governance template JSON (`frai-finetune-plan.json` by default). 137 - `frai finetune validate [--readiness]` – validate a plan and optionally print readiness checkpoints and summaries. 138 139 ### `frai update` 140 Check npm for the latest `frai` release and print upgrade instructions. 141 142 --- 143 144 ## Using `frai-core` (SDK) 145 146 Install from npm: 147 ```bash 148 pnpm add frai-core 149 ``` 150 151 `frai-core` exposes modular helpers that the CLI uses under the hood: 152 - `Questionnaire` – interactive question flows. 153 - `Documents` – generate checklists, model cards, and risk files. 154 - `Scanners` – static analysis for AI indicators. 155 - `Rag` – policy-grounded indexing utilities. 156 - `Eval` – baseline evaluation metrics and report writers. 157 - `Finetune` – governance templates, validation, and readiness scoring. 158 - `Config` & `Providers` – key management and LLM provider wiring. 159 160 Example: generate documentation programmatically. 161 162 ```ts 163 import fs from 'fs/promises'; 164 import inquirer from 'inquirer'; 165 import { Documents, Questionnaire, Scanners } from 'frai-core'; 166 167 const answers = await Questionnaire.runQuestionnaire({ 168 prompt: (questions) => inquirer.prompt(questions) 169 }); 170 171 const { checklist, modelCard, riskFile } = Documents.generateDocuments({ answers }); 172 const scan = Scanners.scanCodebase({ root: process.cwd() }); 173 const aiContext = Documents.buildContextForAITips(answers); 174 175 await fs.writeFile('checklist.md', checklist); 176 await fs.writeFile('model_card.md', modelCard); 177 await fs.writeFile('risk_file.md', riskFile); 178 await fs.writeFile('scan-summary.json', JSON.stringify(scan, null, 2)); 179 await fs.writeFile('ai-context.txt', aiContext); 180 ``` 181 182 Because `frai-core` is a regular ESM package, you can import only the modules you need and embed FRAI capabilities inside automation pipelines, CI jobs, or custom products. 183 184 --- 185 186 ## Local Development 187 188 Clone the repository and work from source: 189 ```bash 190 pnpm install 191 pnpm --filter frai run build 192 node packages/frai-cli/dist/index.js --help 193 ``` 194 195 During development you can install the CLI locally without publishing: 196 ```bash 197 pnpm install --global ./packages/frai-cli 198 # then 199 frai --setup 200 ``` 201 202 Store your OpenAI key by running the CLI setup flow or setting `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `.env`. 203 204 --- 205 206 ## Publishing (Maintainers) 207 208 FRAI ships as two npm packages and they must be published independently. 209 210 1. Bump versions in `packages/frai-core/package.json` and `packages/frai-cli/package.json`. Update the CLI dependency to match the published `frai-core` version (drop `workspace:*`). 211 2. Build the CLI: 212 ```bash 213 pnpm --filter frai run build 214 ``` 215 3. Publish `frai-core` first, then `frai`: 216 ```bash 217 cd packages/frai-core && npm publish 218 cd ../frai-cli && npm publish 219 ``` 220 4. Verify on npm: 221 ```bash 222 npm view frai versions --json 223 npm view frai-core versions --json 224 ``` 225 226 --- 227 228 ## Learn More 229 - Website: [frai.cc](https://frai.cc) 230 - NPM package: [frai](https://www.npmjs.com/package/frai) 231 - docs/ai_feature_backlog.md – roadmap for AI capabilities. 232 - docs/eval_harness_design.md – evaluation harness design notes. 233 - docs/architecture-target.md – monorepo architecture. 234 235 *Framework of Responsible Artificial Intelligence* 236

2	
3	## Overview
4	- Mission: deliver a modular, contribution-friendly responsible AI toolkit spanning CLI, SDKs, guardrails, RAG workflows, and evaluation pipelines.

53	- Publish contributor guidelines, code of conduct, and Phase 1 roadmap issues to invite community participation.

2	
3	## Goals
4	- Provide a lightweight, dependency-free baseline evaluation pipeline developers can run locally.
5	- Standardise reporting so evaluation results feed into documentation, CI, and governance workflows.

18	- Outputs/reference files should be JSON arrays. Each element may be a string or object containing `text`/`output` fields.

22	- `frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js` exposes `DEFAULT_METRICS`; additional metrics can be registered by passing custom evaluators to `runEvaluations`.

## Summary of Findings

### 1. CLI Command Entry Point

**Location:** `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d11/with/h2-eval-thresholds/r2/packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts` (lines 708-717)

```typescript
program
  .command('eval')
  .description('Run evaluation metrics on model outputs.')
  .requiredOption('--outputs <file>', 'Path to JSON file containing model outputs')
  .option('--references <file>', 'Path to JSON file containing reference outputs')
  .option('--report <path>', 'Report path (default: frai-eval-report.json)')
  .option('--format <format>', 'Report format (json or markdown)', 'json')
  .action((options: EvalOptions) => {
    runEvalCommand(options);
  });
```

The `runEvalCommand` function (lines 476-497) orchestrates the evaluation pipeline by:
1. Loading datasets from JSON files using `Eval.loadDataset`
2. Running evaluations with `Eval.runEvaluations`
3. Generating a report with `Eval.generateReport`
4. Writing the report with `Eval.writeReport`

### 2. Metric Definitions

**Location:** `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d11/with/h2-eval-thresholds/r2/packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js`

**Valid Metric IDs and Definitions:**

1. **`exact_match`** - Case-insensitive string comparison between outputs and references
   - Returns: score (0-1), total samples, matches count, per-sample details

2. **`toxicity`** - Keyword scan against default banned terms: 'hate', 'kill', 'violence', 'terrorist', 'racist', 'sexist'
   - Returns: score (safe count / total), total samples, flagged count, flagged sample indices

3. **`length_variance`** - Measures character length differences between outputs and references
   - Returns: score (normalized variance), total samples, average delta, per-sample deltas
   - Score formula: `max(0, 1 - averageDelta / 500)`

All three are exported in `DEFAULT_METRICS` array.

### 3. Evaluation Process Flow

**Location:** `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d11/with/h2-eval-thresholds/r2/packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js`

**Step-by-step:**

1. **Load Dataset** (`loadDataset`)
   - Reads JSON arrays from outputs file (required) and references file (optional)
   - Returns absolute paths and parsed arrays

2. **Run Evaluations** (`runEvaluations`)
   - Takes outputs array, references array, and metrics list
   - Passes outputs and references to each metric function
   - Returns array of metric results with scores and details

3. **Generate Report** (`generateReport`)
   - Wraps evaluations in metadata (timestamp, file paths, total samples)
   - Returns structured report object

4. **Write Report** (`writeReport`)
   - Supports two formats: JSON (default) and Markdown
   - Default filenames: `frai-eval-report.json` or `frai-eval-report.md`
   - Uses `resolveReportPath()` to handle format-specific extensions

**Location:** `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d11/with/h2-eval-thresholds/r2/packages/frai-gate/src/gate/schema.ts` and `validate.ts`

The evaluation section in the responsible AI Gate requires numeric thresholds:
- Schema marks evaluation check with `expectsNumbers: true`
- Validator enforces this: if evaluation section exists but has no digits, it generates a WARNING with message: *"Evaluation plan has no numeric threshold. A check that cannot fail is not a check."*
- Gate template prompts for: **Metrics + thresholds that must pass before shipping** (line 93 of template)

Input files should be JSON arrays where each element is either:
- A plain string: `["output1", "output2"]`
- An object with `text` field: `[{"text": "output1"}, ...]`
- An object with `output` field: `[{"output": "output1"}, ...]`

Output reports include metadata, per-metric results with scores, and sample-level details for debugging.

All files related to evaluation are located in the **`frai-core` package** (the reusable SDK), with CLI integration through **`frai-cli`** for end-user access.

Now I have a comprehensive understanding of the custom metrics system. Let me compile my findings.

## Summary of Custom Metrics in the FRAI SDK

### 1. How Custom Metrics Are Passed to `runEvaluations`

Custom metrics are passed through the `metrics` parameter to `runEvaluations()`:

```javascript
// From /packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js (lines 41-60)
export function runEvaluations({
  outputs,
  references,
  metrics = DEFAULT_METRICS  // <-- Metrics array passed here
} = {}) {
  const outs = ensureArray(outputs);
  const refs = ensureArray(references);

  const evaluations = metrics.map((metric) => {
    if (typeof metric === 'function') {
      return metric(outs, refs);  // <-- Function-based metric
    }
    if (metric && typeof metric.evaluate === 'function') {
      return metric.evaluate(outs, refs);  // <-- Object-based metric
    }
    throw new Error('Invalid metric supplied to runEvaluations.');
  });

  return evaluations;
}
```

Metrics can be:
- **Functions**: `(outputs, references) => metricResult`
- **Objects**: with an `evaluate` method `{ evaluate: (outputs, references) => metricResult }`

### 2. How the Metrics System Handles Unknown Metrics

The system throws an error for invalid metrics:
- If a metric is **not a function** AND
- If it's **not an object** with a `evaluate` function`
- **Result**: `throw new Error('Invalid metric supplied to runEvaluations.')`

There is **no graceful fallback** for unknown metrics—invalid metrics will halt evaluation.

### 3. Where the frai-core SDK Interface is Defined

**Primary file**: `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d11/with/h2-eval-thresholds/r2/packages/frai-core/src/index.js`

This file exports the `Eval` module:
```javascript
export * as Eval from './eval/index.js';
```

The evaluation module itself is at:
- **Core logic**: `/packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js`
- **Metrics definitions**: `/packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js`
- **Report generation**: `/packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js`

- `score`: numeric score or `null` if invalid

Based on my exploration of the codebase, I'll now design a comprehensive implementation plan for adding `--threshold` support to `frai eval`.

## Implementation Plan for `--threshold` Support

### 1. Threshold Validation and Parsing Strategy

**Where**: CLI layer (`packages/frai-cli/src/index.ts`)

**Approach**:
- Add a utility function `parseThresholds(thresholdStrings: string[]): { [metricId: string]: number }`
- Validate format: `<metric>=<number>` using regex `/^([a-z_]+)=([\d.]+)$/`
- Validate range: 0-1 inclusive
- Call this in `runEvalCommand` BEFORE executing evaluations
- If parsing fails, log specific error and `process.exit(2)` immediately

**Rationale**: CLI validates syntax and format (user error), core validates semantic meaning. This provides fast feedback without running evaluations.

**Error Handling Pattern**:
```
Invalid threshold format: "exact_match=foo" (expected <metric>=<number>)
Invalid threshold range: "toxicity=1.5" (must be 0-1)
```

---

### 2. Metric Discovery for Validation/Error Messages

**Challenge**: Validation needs to know valid metric IDs before evaluations run, but custom metrics are user-provided.

**Solution**: Discover valid metrics from `DEFAULT_METRICS` + from evaluations results

**Two-phase approach**:
1. **Pre-evaluation validation**: Check thresholds against known default metric IDs
2. **Post-evaluation validation**: Log warning if threshold was specified for a custom metric that wasn't discovered

**Implementation**:
- In CLI, after parsing thresholds, validate against `DEFAULT_METRICS` IDs (can extract from requiring the core module)
- Pass thresholds to `generateReport`
- In `generateReport`, validate thresholds match the actual evaluated metrics
- Return validation results or errors in report for CLI to handle

**Alternative (simpler)**: Skip pre-evaluation validation, validate all thresholds in `generateReport` against actual metrics. This works with custom metrics automatically.

**Recommended**: Hybrid approach—pre-validate known defaults, allow unknowns (for custom metrics), warn if threshold doesn't match any metric.

---

### 3. Modifying `generateReport()` to Process Thresholds

**Changes to signature**:
```javascript
export function generateReport({
  evaluations,
  outputsPath,
  referencesPath,
  generatedAt = new Date().toISOString(),
  thresholds = {}  // NEW: { metric_id: number, ... }
})
```

**Processing logic**:
1. For each metric in evaluations:
   - If metric has threshold defined and score is not null: `passed = score >= threshold`
   - If metric has threshold but score is null: `passed = false` (no score = failure)
   - If no threshold: `passed = null` (not evaluated)
2. Add to each metric object: `{ passed, threshold }` (threshold value from input)
3. Add to metadata: `{ thresholds: {...}, anyThresholdsFailed: boolean }`

**Return structure**:
```javascript
{
  metadata: {
    generatedAt,
    outputsPath,
    referencesPath,
    totalSamples,
    thresholds: { exact_match: 0.9, ... },  // NEW
    anyThresholdsFailed: true/false          // NEW
  },
  metrics: [
    {
      id, label, score, total, ...,
      threshold: 0.9,   // NEW (if threshold provided)
      passed: true      // NEW (if threshold provided)
    },
    ...
  ]
}
```

---

### 4. CLI Integration and Exit Code Logic

**Flow in `runEvalCommand`**:

```
1. Parse --threshold options → { exact_match: 0.9, ... }
2. Pre-validate thresholds (format, range, warn on unknown metrics)
3. Load dataset
4. Run evaluations
5. Generate report WITH thresholds
6. Determine exit code:
   - 0 if all thresholds passed (or no thresholds)
   - 1 if any threshold failed
   - 2 if validation error (invalid format/range)
7. Write report
8. Log summary and exit
```

**Implementation**:
- Add `threshold?: string[]` to `EvalOptions` (Commander collects multiple `--threshold` into array)
- Create `validateAndParseThresholds()` function
- Create `determineExitCode(report)` function to check `anyThresholdsFailed`
- Call `process.exit(code)` at end of `runEvalCommand`

---

### 5. Report Formatting Changes

**JSON Report (`reporters.js` - `toJson`):**
- No structural change needed, just ensure metadata and metric fields are serialized
- The structure returned from `generateReport` will naturally include thresholds

**Markdown Report (`reporters.js` - `toMarkdown`):**
Add new section after Metrics:
```markdown
## Thresholds

- **exact_match:** 0.9 (actual: 0.85) ❌ FAILED
- **toxicity:** 0.95 (actual: 1.0) ✓ PASSED
- **length_variance:** No threshold

---
```

Or simpler format:
```markdown
## Threshold Results

| Metric | Threshold | Actual | Status |
|--------|-----------|--------|--------|
| Exact Match | 0.9 | 0.85 | FAILED |
| Toxicity | 0.95 | 1.0 | PASSED |
| Length Variance | — | 0.88 | — |
```

---

### 6. Handling Custom Metrics

**Key consideration**: Custom metrics may not be known before evaluation runs.

**Solution**:
- Allow any metric ID in threshold specifications
- In `generateReport`, match thresholds to evaluated metrics by ID
- Thresholds for metrics that don't appear in evaluations are ignored with warning
- All threshold logic remains generic (works for any metric with `id` and `score`)

**Example flow**:
```javascript
// User provides: --threshold custom_score=0.8
// Custom metric returns: { id: 'custom_score', score: 0.75, ... }
// generateReport matches and applies: passed = 0.75 >= 0.8 = false
```

---

### 7. Validation Logic Summary

**In CLI (`runEvalCommand`)**:
- [ ] Parse threshold strings: `metric=number`
- [ ] Validate format (regex match)
- [ ] Validate range (0-1)
- [ ] Warn on unknown default metrics
- [ ] Pass thresholds object to `generateReport`

**In Core (`generateReport`)**:
- [ ] Match thresholds to evaluated metrics by ID
- [ ] Calculate `passed` flag for each threshold
- [ ] Set `anyThresholdsFailed` in metadata
- [ ] Include threshold value in metric result

**In CLI (exit code determination)**:
- [ ] Check `report.metadata.anyThresholdsFailed`
- [ ] Exit 0 if false or no thresholds, exit 1 if true

---

### 8. Backward Compatibility

- Without `--threshold`: thresholds is empty `{}`, all `passed` fields undefined
- Existing reports unaffected (new fields optional)
- Existing tests pass without modification
- Default metric discovery only checks built-in metrics

---

### Implementation Sequence

1. **Phase 1**: Core changes (lowest risk, most reusable)
   - Update `generateReport()` signature and logic
   - Update `toMarkdown()` and `toJson()` formatters
   - Add core unit tests

2. **Phase 2**: CLI integration
   - Add `threshold` to `EvalOptions` interface
   - Implement `parseThresholds()` validation function
   - Update `runEvalCommand()` to parse, validate, and pass thresholds
   - Implement `determineExitCode()` function
   - Update CLI error handling for exit code 2

3. **Phase 3**: Integration testing
   - Test full CLI flow with various threshold combinations
   - Test error cases (invalid format, out of range)
   - Test with custom metrics
   - Test backward compatibility

Currently, `frai eval` always exits 0, preventing CI pipelines from gating on evaluation metrics. This feature adds optional threshold checking so CI can fail when metrics fall below configurable minimums.

Add `--threshold <metric>=<min>` CLI option (repeatable) and threshold validation to report generation:

- **Fail**: metric score < threshold, OR metric has no score (null)

frai eval --outputs data.json --threshold exact_match=0.9
